# Question 1

## Question 1.1

Let $G_1 = \{j:X_j=0\}$ and $G_2 = \{j:X_j=1\}$, where $\sum_{j \in G_1}=n_1$ and 
$\sum_{j \in G_2}$ = n_2$. The model gives


$$
\mu_1=\beta_0,\qquad \mu_2=\beta_0+\beta^*.
$$

$$
H_0:\mu_1=\mu_2 \equiv H_0:\beta^*=0.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}
L(\beta_0,\beta^*,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_2^2)
&=\prod_{j\in G_1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_1^2}}
\exp\left\{-\frac{(Y_j-\beta_0)^2}{2\sigma_1^2}\right\}\prod_{j\in G_2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma_2^2}}
\exp\left\{-\frac{(Y_j-\beta_0-\beta^*)^2}{2\sigma_2^2}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell(\beta_0,\beta^*,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_2^2)
&=-\frac{n_1+n_2}{2}\log(2\pi)
-\frac{n_1}{2}\log(\sigma_1^2)
-\frac{n_2}{2}\log(\sigma_2^2)-\frac{1}{2\sigma_1^2}\sum_{j\in G_1}(Y_j-\beta_0)^2
-\frac{1}{2\sigma_2^2}\sum_{j\in G_2}(Y_j-\beta_0-\beta^*)^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Treating $\sigma_1^2$ and $\sigma_2^2$ as known, the score equations are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\beta_0}
&=\frac{1}{\sigma_1^2}\sum_{j\in G_1}(Y_j-\beta_0)
+\frac{1}{\sigma_2^2}\sum_{j\in G_2}(Y_j-\beta_0-\beta^*),\\
\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\beta^*}
&=\frac{1}{\sigma_2^2}\sum_{j\in G_2}(Y_j-\beta_0-\beta^*).
\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the scores to zero gives

$$
\widehat\beta_0=\overline Y_1,
\qquad \widehat\beta^*=\overline Y_2-\overline Y_1.
$$

The negative Hessian, which is also the Fisher information for $(\beta_0,\beta^*)^T$, is

$$
I=\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{n_1}{\sigma_1^2}+\dfrac{n_2}{\sigma_2^2} & \dfrac{n_2}{\sigma_2^2}\\[8pt]
\dfrac{n_2}{\sigma_2^2} & \dfrac{n_2}{\sigma_2^2}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
With the equation of invertion 
$$
V =
\begin{pmatrix}
a & b \\
b & c
\end{pmatrix}^{-1}
=
\frac{1}{ac-b^2}
\begin{pmatrix}
c & -b \\
-b & a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad ac-b^2 \neq 0.
$$

$$
I^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{\sigma_1^2}{n_1} & -\dfrac{\sigma_1^2}{n_1}\\
-\dfrac{\sigma_1^2}{n_1} & \dfrac{\sigma_1^2}{n_1}+\dfrac{\sigma_2^2}{n_2}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$



Thus Wald statistic is

$$
Z_W=\frac{\widehat\beta^*}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\beta^*)}}
=\frac{\overline Y_2-\overline Y_1}
{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2/n_1+\sigma_2^2/n_2}}.
$$


$$
W=Z_W^2=\frac{(\overline Y_2-\overline Y_1)^2}
{\sigma_1^2/n_1+\sigma_2^2/n_2}.
$$


## Question 1.2

$$
S_g=\sum_{j\in G_g}(Y_j-\overline Y_g)^2, g=1,2.
$$

$$
\widehat\beta_0=\overline Y_1, \ 
\widehat\beta^*=\overline Y_2-\overline Y_1, \
\widehat\sigma_{g,\mathrm{ML}}^2=\frac{S_g}{n_g}.
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{\mathrm{ML}}
&=
\frac{(\widehat\beta^*)^2}
{\widehat\sigma_{1,\mathrm{ML}}^2/n_1+
 \widehat\sigma_{2,\mathrm{ML}}^2/n_2}\\
&=
\frac{(\overline Y_2-\overline Y_1)^2}
{S_1/n_1^2+S_2/n_2^2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

plug in:

$$
s_g^2=\frac{S_g}{n_g-1}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z^2
&=
\frac{(\overline Y_2-\overline Y_1)^2}
{s_1^2/n_1+s_2^2/n_2}\\
&=
\frac{(\overline Y_2-\overline Y_1)^2}
{S_1/[n_1(n_1-1)]+S_2/[n_2(n_2-1)]}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
W_{\mathrm{ML}}\ne Z^2
$$


For any finite n_1,n_2.

$$
W_{\mathrm{Wald}}(s_1^2,s_2^2)
=
\frac{(\widehat\beta^*)^2}{s_1^2/n_1+s_2^2/n_2}
=
Z^2.
$$

The difference vanishes asymptotically as both group sizes grow. Equal group sizes alone do not make the finite-sample statistics equal.

$$
\frac{\widehat\sigma_{g,\mathrm{ML}}^2}{s_g^2}
=
\frac{n_g-1}{n_g}
\longrightarrow 1
\quad n_g\longrightarrow\infty.
$$


# Question 2

For $X_j=0$, let $p_1=\beta_0$. 

For $X_j=1$, let $p_2=\beta_0+\beta^*$. 

$$
H_0:p_1=p_2 \
\equiv \
H_0:\beta^*=0.
$$

Let $G_1=\{j:X_j=0\}$ and $G_2=\{j:X_j=1\}$. The likelihood is

$$
\begin{aligned}
L(\beta_0,\beta^*)&=
\prod_{j\in G_1}
\beta_0^{Y_j}(1-\beta_0)^{1-Y_j}
\prod_{j\in G_2}
(\beta_0+\beta^*)^{Y_j}
(1-\beta_0-\beta^*)^{1-Y_j}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The log-likelihood is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell(\beta_0,\beta^*)
&=
\sum_{j\in G_1}
\left[
Y_j\log(\beta_0)
+(1-Y_j)\log(1-\beta_0)
\right]+
\sum_{j\in G_2}
\left[
Y_j\log(\beta_0+\beta^*)
+(1-Y_j)\log(1-\beta_0-\beta^*)
\right]
\end{aligned}
$$


$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\beta_0}
&=
\sum_{j\in G_1}\frac{Y_j-p_1}{p_1(1-p_1)}
+
\sum_{j\in G_2}\frac{Y_j-p_2}{p_2(1-p_2)},\\
\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\beta^*}
&=
\sum_{j\in G_2}\frac{Y_j-p_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Setting both scores to zero yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
\widehat p_1
&=\frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{j=1}^{n_1+n_2}(1-X_j)Y_j,\\
\widehat p_2
&=\frac{1}{n_2}\sum_{j=1}^{n_1+n_2}X_jY_j,\\
\widehat\beta_0&=\widehat p_1, \\
\widehat\beta^* &=\widehat p_2-\widehat p_1.
\end{aligned}
$$


The Fisher information matrix is

$$
I(\beta_0,\beta^*)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{n_1}{p_1(1-p_1)}
+\dfrac{n_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}
&
\dfrac{n_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}
\\[10pt]
\dfrac{n_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}
&
\dfrac{n_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

With the equation of invertion 

$$
V =
\begin{pmatrix}
a & b \\
b & c
\end{pmatrix}^{-1}
=
\frac{1}{ac-b^2}
\begin{pmatrix}
c & -b \\
-b & a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad ac-b^2 \neq 0.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
I(\beta_0,\beta^*)^{-1}
&=
\frac{p_1(1-p_1)p_2(1-p_2)}{n_1n_2}
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{n_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}
&
-\dfrac{n_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}
\\[10pt]
-\dfrac{n_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}
&
\dfrac{n_1}{p_1(1-p_1)}
+\dfrac{n_2}{p_2(1-p_2)}
\end{pmatrix}
\\[12pt]
&=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{p_1(1-p_1)}{n_1}
&
-\dfrac{p_1(1-p_1)}{n_1}
\\[10pt]
-\dfrac{p_1(1-p_1)}{n_1}
&
\dfrac{p_1(1-p_1)}{n_1}
+\dfrac{p_2(1-p_2)}{n_2}
\end{pmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the variance function is:

$$
\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\widehat\beta^*)
=
\frac{\widehat p_1(1-\widehat p_1)}{n_1}
+
\frac{\widehat p_2(1-\widehat p_2)}{n_2}.
$$

The Wald statistic for \(H_0:\beta^*=0\) is

$$
\begin{aligned}
W
&=
\frac{(\widehat\beta^*)^2}
{\widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\widehat\beta^*)}\\[6pt]
&=
\frac{(\widehat p_2-\widehat p_1)^2}
{
\widehat p_1(1-\widehat p_1)/n_1
+
\widehat p_2(1-\widehat p_2)/n_2
} \\
& \equiv Z^2
\end{aligned}
$$

This is exactly the $W \equiv Z^2$ statistic specified in the question. 
Under $H_0$ and the usual large-sample regularity conditions, $W$ has an asymptotic $\chi^2_1$ distribution, so as $Z^2$.

# Question 4




# Question 5

Let $Y_j \sim \operatorname{Binomial}(n_j,p_j)$ independently for groups $j=1,2$. Under the log-link model,

$$
p_1=\exp(\beta_0), \qquad
p_2=\exp(\beta_0+\beta^*).
$$

We test $H_0:\beta^*=0$ against $H_A:\beta^*\ne 0$. This is equivalent to testing $p_1=p_2$. Define

$$
\hat p_1=\frac{Y_1}{n_1}, \qquad
\hat p_2=\frac{Y_2}{n_2}, \qquad
\tilde p=\frac{Y_1+Y_2}{n_1+n_2}.
$$

The unrestricted maximum likelihood estimate is
$\hat\beta^*=\log(\hat p_2/\hat p_1)$. The Fisher information matrix and its inverse are

$$
I(\beta_0,\beta^*)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{n_1p_1}{1-p_1}+\dfrac{n_2p_2}{1-p_2}
&
\dfrac{n_2p_2}{1-p_2}\\[8pt]
\dfrac{n_2p_2}{1-p_2}
&
\dfrac{n_2p_2}{1-p_2}
\end{pmatrix}
$$

and

$$
I(\beta_0,\beta^*)^{-1}=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{1-p_1}{n_1p_1}
&
-\dfrac{1-p_1}{n_1p_1}\\[8pt]
-\dfrac{1-p_1}{n_1p_1}
&
\dfrac{1-p_1}{n_1p_1}+\dfrac{1-p_2}{n_2p_2}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

### a. Wald test

The lower-right entry of $I^{-1}$ gives the estimated variance of
$\hat\beta^*$. Therefore, the Wald statistic is

$$
W=\frac{\left[\log(\hat p_2/\hat p_1)\right]^2}
{\dfrac{1-\hat p_1}{n_1\hat p_1}
+\dfrac{1-\hat p_2}{n_2\hat p_2}}.
$$

### b. Score test

Under $H_0$, both groups have the common probability $\tilde p$.
After accounting for the nuisance parameter $\beta_0$, the efficient
score and its information are

$$
U_{\mathrm{eff}}
=\frac{Y_2-n_2\tilde p}{1-\tilde p},
\qquad
I_{\mathrm{eff}}
=\frac{n_1n_2\tilde p}
{(n_1+n_2)(1-\tilde p)}.
$$

Hence the score statistic simplifies to

$$
S=\frac{U_{\mathrm{eff}}^2}{I_{\mathrm{eff}}} =
\frac{(\hat p_2-\hat p_1)^2}
{\tilde p(1-\tilde p)(1/n_1+1/n_2)}.
$$

### c. Likelihood ratio test

The unrestricted model uses $\hat p_1$ and $\hat p_2$; the model under
$H_0$ uses $\tilde p$ for both groups. Twice the difference between
their maximized log likelihoods is

$$
G^2
=
2\sum_{j=1}^{2}
\left[
Y_j\log\left(\frac{\hat p_j}{\tilde p}\right)
+
(n_j-Y_j)
\log\left(\frac{1-\hat p_j}{1-\tilde p}\right)
\right]
$$

Under $H_0$, each of $W$, $S$, and $G^2$ has an asymptotic
$\chi^2_1$ distribution. At significance level 0.05, reject $H_0$
when the chosen statistic exceeds 3.841. The formulas above assume
interior estimated probabilities ($0<\hat p_1,\hat p_2,\tilde p<1$).
